claim: Google launches Gemini Decision 1, a model that scores answers instead of writing them

support.quote: Today, we’re introducing the Gemini Decisions API, a new endpoint for fast, closed-set decisions powered by our new Gemini Decision 1 model (gemini-decision-1), available through the Gemini API in Google AI Studio.

claim: The new Gemini Decisions API answers yes/no, multiple-choice and rubric questions with probabilities, at $0.10 per million input tokens and no charge for output.

support.quote: Today, we’re introducing the Gemini Decisions API, a new endpoint for fast, closed-set decisions powered by our new Gemini Decision 1 model (gemini-decision-1), available through the Gemini API in Google AI Studio.

claim: Google DeepMind introduced the Gemini Decisions API on November 11, 2026, a new endpoint for what it calls "fast, closed-set decisions", powered by a new model named Gemini Decision 1.

support.quote: Today, we’re introducing the Gemini Decisions API, a new endpoint for fast, closed-set decisions powered by our new Gemini Decision 1 model (gemini-decision-1), available through the Gemini API in Google AI Studio.

claim: The API accepts three kinds of question: yes/no checks, multiple choice among 2 to 255 options, and scores on an ordered rubric.

support.quote: Gemini Notebook uses the Decisions API as a real-time router to instantly direct incoming queries to the optimal model tier and thinking level for each request.

claim: One request carries a single shared input of up to 256K tokens, which can mix text, images, audio, video and PDFs, along with up to 1,000 independent questions.

support.quote: You can pass one multimodal input across text, images, audio, video, and PDFs (up to 256K tokens) along with up to 1,000 independent questions.

claim: The two headline limits share one budget: the documentation gives a context window of "262,144 tokens across shared input and all questions", so a request cannot carry both a full-size input and a very long list of questions.

support.quote: 262,144 tokens across shared input and all questions

claim: Every answer comes with a confidence score from 0 to 1 so that, in Google's words, "your code can route ambiguous cases to a fallback or human reviewer".

support.quote: Every answer includes a confidence score (from 0 to 1) so your code can route ambiguous cases to a fallback or human reviewer

claim: SiliconANGLE gives the example of a security team asking the model to rate the severity of an antivirus alert on a scale of 1 to 10.

support.quote: A cybersecurity team, for example, could ask the model to rate the severity of an antivirus alert on a scale of 1 to 10.

claim: Gemini Decision 1 costs $0.10 per 1M input tokens, and output is not billed, because the model generates no output tokens.

support.quote: Gemini Decision 1 is priced at $0.10 per 1M input tokens and $0 for output tokens, with an API no-cost tier you can use in Google AI Studio for prototyping.

claim: Google says this makes the model "nearly 5x cheaper across the shared benchmark suite" than Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, which SiliconANGLE describes as Google's entry-level language model.

support.quote: With zero output tokens billed, Gemini Decision 1 with the Decisions API is nearly 5x cheaper across the shared benchmark suite than Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite with the Interactions API.

claim: That is not what Google's post says: it gives the price, and OpenRouter lists the model at $0.10 per million input tokens with free output.

support.quote: Gemini Decision 1 is priced at $0.10 per 1M input tokens and $0 for output tokens, with an API no-cost tier you can use in Google AI Studio for prototyping.

claim: MLQ.ai notes that $0.10 per million input tokens is also what Meta charges for Muse Ember, "its small model for high-volume agent work", although Muse Ember generates text and Gemini Decision 1 does not.

support.quote: The price matches the $0.10 per million input tokens Meta set for Muse Ember, its small model for high-volume agent work (MLQ.ai coverage), although Muse Ember is a text generator.

claim: Google reports an end-to-end latency of 150 to 250 milliseconds.

support.quote: keeping median latency 50-100 ms of model compute (150-250 ms end-to-end), across multimodal inputs and contexts up to 16K tokens, remaining nearly flat from 1 to 100 questions per request

claim: The figure comes with a condition: it was measured on "contexts up to 16K tokens", far below the 256K maximum, and with 1 to 100 questions per request rather than 1,000.

support.quote: keeping median latency 50-100 ms of model compute (150-250 ms end-to-end), across multimodal inputs and contexts up to 16K tokens, remaining nearly flat from 1 to 100 questions per request

claim: The model is available now, under the identifier gemini-decision-1, through the Gemini API in Google AI Studio.

support.quote: Today, we’re introducing the Gemini Decisions API, a new endpoint for fast, closed-set decisions powered by our new Gemini Decision 1 model (gemini-decision-1), available through the Gemini API in Google AI Studio.

claim: The documentation lists it on the Gemini Developer API (v1beta) only, and notes that context caching and the Batch API are not supported.

support.quote: Available on the Gemini Developer API (v1beta) with Gemini Decision 1 only.

claim: Crypto Briefing gives the only precise dates for the rivals: OpenAI's Decisions API "entered public beta on October 6, 2026", and Microsoft followed on October 9, 2026 with a model called Microsoft-Decision-1.

support.quote: OpenAI’s Decisions API entered public beta on October 6, 2026. Microsoft followed on October 9, 2026, with a model called Microsoft-Decision-1.

claim: On performance, Google's post says only that Gemini Decision 1 "leads across the suite, with the lowest calibration error".

support.quote: On benchmarks spanning agent routing, reasoning, ranking, and multimodal understanding, Gemini Decision 1 leads across the suite, with the lowest calibration error.

claim: The rival dates hold up: OpenAI's API changelog lists its Decisions API in beta on October 6, 2026 and as generally available on October 22, 2026.

support.quote: Oct 6 Feature gpt-6-luna v1/decisions Released the Decisions API in beta with gpt-6-luna.

claim: Microsoft's post putting Microsoft-Decision-1 in public preview is dated October 9, 2026.

support.quote: Now available in public preview, Microsoft-Decision-1 is a decision model built on Qwen3.5-9B and designed for applications that need to make fast, structured choices among predefined options.
